name: Coruscation Mage
description:
{2}: Create a token that's a copy of this creature.

Whenever you cast a spell, this creature deals damage to each opponent.
assumptions: Rendered node C's cond:token + thing:self as "Create a token that's a copy of this creature" — the node establishes that a token copy of the card's own identity enters the battlefield for {2}, but the exact verb/phrasing isn't itself fixed by the schema.
Assumed the damage in D→E is dealt by this creature (the ability's own source), since no other source is named on node E.
Rendered trigger-type "spellcast" with thing: any as unrestricted "Whenever you cast a spell" (not limited to instant/sorcery), since any denotes an unspecified card rather than a restricted type.
Assumed node E's owner: opp phrasing is "each opponent" rather than "target opponent," since node E carries no target flag.
couldNotDerive: The amount of damage dealt to each opponent — node E has no qty flag, so no number is given.
Any restriction on the {2} activated ability (once-per-turn limiter, sorcery-speed clause, tap cost) — none present on node C beyond the {2} mana cost.
notes: Two real translator/decomposition gaps, both confirmed against forge-model/data/coruscation-mage.txt's real oracle text ("Offspring {2}... Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent."): (1) Offspring's own `cost:{2}` flag on an `enters` node is genuinely ambiguous with an activated ability's cost — nothing in the node distinguishes "pay this once, at cast time, for a conditional ETB" from "pay this any time, repeatedly, for an immediate effect"; the examiner reasonably read it as the latter. Offspring needs a flag distinguishing an alternate/additional cast-time cost from a true activated-ability cost. (2) The SpellCast trigger's `ValidCard$ Card.nonCreature` qualifier was lost entirely — the translator's ValidCard-clause parser (built for ChangesZone-style "self or another Cat entering" predicates, per this session's Arahbo work) doesn't understand a coarse-type-with-negation filter on a *different* trigger type (which spell you cast, not which permanent enters), so it fell back to `thing: any`, and "noncreature" never made it into the data at all. Root cause is a genuine gap in app/lib/forgeTranslate.ts's trigger predicate handling, not examiner error — a second blind attempt against the same node data would reproduce the identical gaps, so not retried. Separately, node E's real NumDmg$1 was correctly omitted from qty per SCHEMA's own "default 1" convention, but the exam packet's own schema summary (shared with make-exam.mjs) doesn't restate that default explicitly, so the examiner reasonably flagged it as undeterminable — a packet-completeness issue worth fixing in both scripts, not a data gap.
